module_summary: filer_copy.c is the classic uLE recursive copy() used by every browser paste (normal, rename, PSU backup/restore, Move), with a Move manifest that deletes sources only after verification, per-device stat/attribute restoration (mc, vmc, xfrom, fileXio) and a diagnostic context for failure messages; chunks run on the dashboard worker. filer_device.c decides which IOP driver stacks a path needs and refuses incompatible source/destination pairs. filer_fileops.c holds the gen* fileXio wrappers (path normalisation for host/cf/mc, error normalisation for MCMAN and FatFs, no-replace rename) plus a large FILEOP_TRACE debug layer. filer_mount.c manages pfs/dvr_pfs mount slots. ftp_session.c is the EE side of the ps2ftpd control RPC. gui.c holds the classic ynDialog/nonDialog/keyboard, which the dashboard overrides except at launch time. gui_colors.h only declares two CNF helpers.

reusable_helpers.name: genLimObjName
reusable_helpers.what: truncates the last path component to 32 (mc/vmc) or 256 chars, keeping the extension and a trailing slash

reusable_helpers.name: genGetStat
reusable_helpers.what: fileXioGetStat with host/cf/mc path mapping and MCMAN/FatFs error normalisation

reusable_helpers.name: genRenameNoReplace
reusable_helpers.what: same-folder rename that refuses to replace and verifies the result, including mc/xfrom via SetFileInfo

reusable_helpers.name: genOpen
reusable_helpers.what: fileXioOpen with path mapping and a dev:/path vs dev:path retry

reusable_helpers.name: ensurePathDeviceStackReady
reusable_helpers.what: loads the IOP driver stack a device path needs (usb, mmce, mx4sio, ilink, ata, cf, hdd, dvrp, cdfs, host, udpfs, smb)

reusable_helpers.name: prepareTransferDeviceStacks
reusable_helpers.what: readies source and destination stacks and rejects pairs that cannot be loaded together

reusable_helpers.name: mountParty
reusable_helpers.what: mounts an HDD partition on a free or reclaimable pfsN: slot

reusable_helpers.name: filerGetGameTitle
reusable_helpers.what: reads a save title from icon.sys, a PS1 save header or a .psu

reusable_helpers.name: listingSum
reusable_helpers.what: order-independent FNV-1a sum of the names in a directory listing

reusable_helpers.name: ynDialog
reusable_helpers.what: classic yes/no dialog with dashboard override hook

findings.title: FILEOP_TRACE debug tracing is never compiled: ULE_DEBUG_BUILD is defined by no build
findings.problem: Every #if FILEOP_TRACE block (24 in filer_copy.c, 33 in filer_fileops.c incl. a 143-line fd-tracking table, 6 in filer_mount.c) depends on ULE_DEBUG_BUILD, which neither ps2.yaml, configure_ds34.py, scripts nor workflows define, so FILEOP_TRACE is always 0. filer.c:156-163 even defines FILEOP_TRACE and never tests it.
findings.fix: Delete the four ULE_DEBUG_BUILD/FILEOP_TRACE preambles, every #if FILEOP_TRACE block (keeping the #else side where there is one, e.g. filer_fileops.c:571-573 and 702-704), and the trace_* locals in copy(); drop the ULE_DEBUG_BUILD suffix branch in launchelf.h. Update tests/test_copy_short_io.py:58, which slices copy() on '#if FILEOP_TRACE'.
findings.benefit: ~507 source lines (MEASURED by counting the #if FILEOP_TRACE blocks: 141 in filer_copy.c, 316 in filer_fileops.c, 18 in filer_mount.c, plus 4 x 8-line preambles); no ELF change since the preprocessor already drops it (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Grep ULE_DEBUG_BUILD|FILEOP_TRACE over src/Launchstation: only filer_copy.c, filer_fileops.c, filer_mount.c, filer.c, launchelf.h:11 and tests (test_copy_pipeline.py:46, test_copy_psu_listing.py:62, test_listing_callers.py:58 #define FILEOP_TRACE 0; test_copy_short_io.py:58 string slice). Grep DEBUG_BUILD over *.yaml,*.yml,*.py,*.sh,*.md: no files. filer.c has FILEOP_TRACE only at 157-162 (definitions). Block line counts from a script that walked each #if FILEOP_TRACE to its matching #endif.

findings.title: copy() builds the classic text progress report and speed/ETA stats every chunk, but the dashboard progress always replaces it
findings.problem: Each chunk computes speed/ETA (1454-1480) and formats a ~15-sprintf/strcat report into progress (1482-1531), used only when DashFileProgress returns 0 (1534-1540). DashFileProgress returns 0 only when the dashboard is inactive or on the worker thread (dash_ui.c:1431); copy() is only called from subfunc_Paste (filer_browser.c:2208), reached from the dashboard browser on the UI thread (dash_browser.c:892-894) while DashRun, which never returns, keeps dash_active=1.
findings.fix: Delete the speed/ETA computation, the progress text, calcTransferSpeed/calcRemainingTime/smoothTransferSpeed, TRANSFER_ETA_UPDATE_MS, the related locals, PasteProgress_f, written_size and PasteTime; keep the DashFileProgress call and use its result only to choose the worker chunk path. Update the helper-name lists in tests/test_copy_pipeline.py:221, test_copy_psu_listing.py:282, test_listing_callers.py:246. The five LNG strings (Remain_Size, Current_Speed, Remain_Time, Written_Total, Average_Speed) then become unused in Lang/*.LNG and Lang/DASHBOARD.inc.
findings.benefit: ~135 source lines; removes ~15 sprintf/strcat and 3 divisions per chunk on the UI thread; a few hundred bytes of .text (INFERRED, not measured).
findings.evidence: Read dash_ui.c:1428-1466 (DashFileProgress returns 0 only for !DashIsActive() || dashWorkerOnThread()); dash_main.c:190-193, 314-318, 1349 (dash_active set in DashRun, cleared only by DashStopUiForExec at exec). Grep 'copy(' callers: only filer_browser.c:2208 plus recursion; subfunc_Paste callers filer_browser.c:2287/2305/2324, entry points used from dash_browser.c:892,894,1015. Grep LNG(Remain_Size|Current_Speed|Remain_Time|Written_Total|Average_Speed): only filer_copy.c. Grep written_size|PasteTime|PasteProgress_f: only the cited lines. INFERRED part: that no classic browser paste can run while the dashboard is inactive.

findings.title: copy() repeats the per-device stat/attribute restoration for folders and files, each with an empty if-else chain
findings.problem: The folder closure (1225-1276) and file closure (1639-1691) are the same mc/vmc/xfrom/fileXio dispatch differing only in MC_ATTR_norm_folder vs MC_ATTR_norm_file, an mctype_PSx==2 check and an mmce skip (missing from the folder copy). Both use a 5-branch if/else-if chain whose bodies are empty just to skip fileXioChStat; the PSU_RESTORE closure 1277-1287 repeats the same mc/vmc/xfrom dispatch a third time.
findings.fix: Make one static function that applies copied stats to 'out' given 'in', the stats and the normal attribute value, with the skip list as a single condition (host, udpfs, smb, mmce, mass, mx4sio, ata, cf), and call it from both closures; reuse it for the PSU_RESTORE folder fix-up.
findings.benefit: ~45 source lines (INFERRED: two ~52-line blocks plus an 11-line block become one ~30-line function and three calls); also gives folders the same mmce skip as files.
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:1225-1287 and 1639-1691 side by side. Differences: 1230 vs 1643 attribute constant; 1240 vs 1653-1658 (mctype_PSx check); 1673 mmce branch only in the file closure. Host tests extract copy() whole (test_copy_pipeline.py, test_copy_psu_listing.py, test_listing_callers.py), so they exercise the result.

findings.title: Same path-preparation preamble copied into six gen* wrappers in filer_fileops.c
findings.problem: genRmdir, genRemove, genGetStat, genMkdir, genOpen and genDopen each repeat: check cf online, copy the path into a local MAX_PATH buffer, makeHostPath, ensurePathMemoryCardAccessible, normalizePcCardCfPath, genLimObjName (genDopen omits the last). genRmdir, genRemove and genDopen use a second MAX_PATH buffer for makeHostPath although genGetStat/genMkdir/genOpen show it works in place.
findings.fix: Add one static helper that fills a caller buffer from a path with these steps and returns -ENODEV when the CF card is offline (with a flag to skip genLimObjName for genDopen), and call it from the six wrappers; drop the extra mapped_path buffers.
findings.justification: The same 8-12 lines appear six times; one ~14-line helper plus six 2-line calls removes code and one MAX_PATH stack buffer in three wrappers.
findings.benefit: ~30 source lines (INFERRED: 6 x ~9 lines replaced by 6 x 2 plus a 14-line helper); one fewer MAX_PATH stack buffer in genRmdir/genRemove/genDopen.
findings.evidence: Read all six functions in filer_fileops.c. makeHostPath used in place at 371, 510, 548 and into a separate buffer at 234, 273, 627. Order differences (cf check before/after makeHostPath) do not matter since a cf path is never a host path (INFERRED).

findings.title: copy() re-runs prepareTransferDeviceStacks at every recursion level although subfunc_Paste already did it
findings.problem: subfunc_Paste prepares both stacks once (filer_browser.c:2164) and copy() prepares them again for every file and folder (804). Each call re-walks all path checks and ensurePathDeviceStackReady; for host: that is initHOST() (filer.c:1720-1734), which opens host:elflist.txt and dopens host: over the network for every copied entry.
findings.fix: Call prepareTransferDeviceStacks in copy() only when recurses == 0 (or rely on subfunc_Paste's call and delete it from copy()); update tests/test_transfer_stack_preflight.py:176-177, which assert the call is in copy().
findings.benefit: ~2 host RPCs saved per copied entry on host:, fewer string compares elsewhere; ~6 lines (INFERRED, not measured).
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:804, filer_browser.c:2156-2217 (only copy() caller), filer_device.c:105-228, filer.c:1720-1734 (initHOST). tests/test_copy_pipeline.py:113 models an IOP reset during preflight; whether a reset can happen between two entries of one paste was not traced (INFERRED).

findings.title: genOpen retries every failed open with the other dev:/path spelling
findings.problem: After any failed fileXioOpen, genOpen rewrites dev:/path to dev:path (or back) and opens again, so every expected failure (probing for a missing file, O_CREAT in a missing folder, verifyUdpfsCopy) costs a second IOP or network round trip. No caller or comment names a device that needs the alternate spelling; the code dates from the fork's initial commit 944a2fc.
findings.fix: Delete the fallback after checking on hardware which device, if any, still needs it; if one does, limit the retry to that device prefix.
findings.benefit: ~36 source lines; one fewer IOP RPC per failed open (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read filer_fileops.c:531-611. git log -S 'Path-style compatibility fallback' -- src/: only 944a2fc (initial commit). Which devices accept only one spelling was not verified.

findings.title: Same dialog message split/measure/centre block in ynDialog, nonDialog and main_exploit_installer ok_result_dialog
findings.problem: Three copies of the same ~19 lines: split the message at newlines, measure the widest line with printXY, clamp to 96 and compute dh/dw/dx/dy (nonDialog uses 16*n, the others FONT_HEIGHT*(n+1)).
findings.fix: Move the split-and-measure loop into one helper in gui.c (returning the line count and width) and call it from the three dialogs.
findings.justification: Three identical copies; a ~12-line helper and three 1-2 line calls remove code.
findings.benefit: ~25 source lines (INFERRED: 3 x ~13 duplicated lines replaced by a 12-line helper and 3 calls).
findings.evidence: Read gui.c:10-141 and main_exploit_installer.c:792-839; duplicate-block leads gui.c:20-35 == gui.c:111-126 and gui.c:22-40 == main_exploit_installer.c:807-825 confirmed. The classic dialogs stay live: dash_main.c:668 uninstalls the dashboard overrides for launch-time prompts.

findings.title: Small redundancies in filer_copy.c, filer_mount.c and filer_device.c
findings.problem: copyDiagFail(ret) runs twice on the normal exit (1697, 1702), and the copy_file_exit_mem_err label (used only at 1425, where buff and buff2 are NULL) is unnecessary; copy_diag.total is set at 1361 and again at 1395; iox_stat.attr = 0 at 1112 is a dead store; the 85-89 comment says LaunchELF is single-threaded though chunks now run on the worker, and 119-120 is an orphan comment for psu_restore_buff (declared at 272); unmountParty re-tests party_ix < MOUNT_LIMIT after rejecting it at 94; unmountAll clears mountedDVRPParty[i][0] behind a needless test; filer_device.c re-declares host_error that filer_internal.h:12 already declares; latestDVRPMount is declared in both launchelf.h:571 and filer_internal.h:8.
findings.fix: Delete the duplicate call, label and goto target (use copy_file_exit), the second total assignment, the dead store, the stale/orphan comments, the redundant tests and the duplicate extern declarations.
findings.benefit: ~20 source lines; no measurable ELF change (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read the cited lines. free(NULL) is safe, so jumping to copy_file_exit from 1425 frees nothing extra (buff NULL, buff2 not yet allocated; for PSU_RESTORE buff==psu_restore_buff is skipped). Grep extern host_error / latestDVRPMount: filer_internal.h:8,12, launchelf.h:571, filer_device.c:14; filer_device.c includes filer_internal.h at line 4.
